Prevention: Take soil to be tested for calcium deficiency @ KALRO Kabete, Soilcare or
KEPHIS If soil test results indicate acidity in soil, reduce use of ammonium fertilizers e.g.
DAP (diammonium phosphate), urea, ASN (ammonium sulphate nitrate), and instead use neutral and basic fertilizers, e.g.
N:P:K, CAN (calcium ammonium nitrate), TSP (triple super phosphate), SSP (single super phosphate) and
Apply lime at least 3 months before planting.
Once lime has been applied, use of ammonium fertilizer can begin
Apply lime once every 4 years @ 2 tonnes/ha (800kg/acre
Broadcast and mix with the soil during land preparation
Monitoring: Check out symptoms in younger leaves and growing points.
Look out for death of growing points, leaf distortion, leaf scorching, leaves folding downwards and failure of leaf margins to expand
Check for aborted flowers and dying growing points
Look for water-soaked discoloration in fruits (blossom end rot) common in tomatoes, Capsicum, peppers and watermelon
Direct Control: Use foliar feeds below to correct deficiency symtoms on growing crop to improve crop appearance
CAN incase crop has not flowered @ 50kg/acre
Restrictions: Always put on protective clothing when applying fertilizers
Wash protective gear after fertilizer application
Store protective gear separate from household appliances
Do not store fertilizer directly on the floor
Apply lime once every 4 years before planting in the field.
In greenhouses, apply calcium foliar feed when deficiency symptoms are observed
